To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
natural evolution is not a good model for directed evolution.

(i) there are many more reasons why natural evolution cannot find the optimal individual than those stated in the commentary and (ii) the operators and selection schemes of directed evolution, which are the same as the operators and selection of in silico evolution, can be implemented in the laboratory.
natural evolution cannot find the optimal individual and directed evolution, using the methods of evolutionary algorithms, can find the optimal individual.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of in vitro and in vivo evolution experiments that can be performed with the same operators and selection schemes as those used by in silico evolution.
how to make directed evolution more efficient, more precise, more predictable, and more reliable.
the application of evolutionary algorithms to directed evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
directed evolution can be used to do anything that natural evolution can do and more.
natural evolution cannot find or select the optimal individual.
directed evolution is a much better way to find the ‘optimal individual’ than natural evolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methods and operators of natural evolution are limited and that the methods and schemes of synthetic biology can do better.
the commentary of Whingham and colleagues is not only wrong in many respects but also misleading in its title.
natural evolution is not optimal, but directed evolution is.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the methods of evolutionary computation can be used for the design of synthetic biology programmes.
the methods of synthetic and directed evolution can be applied to the design of any system, including the design of evolutionary systems themselves.
directed evolution can be made to be more effective by using synthetic biology to make directed evolution as much like natural evolution as possible.
